title: North End traffic stop leads to seizure of two firearms – three in custody: C26-3249
content:
On January 5, 2026, North District General Patrol and Community Support Unit officers arrested three individuals following a traffic stop involving a 2020 Ford Explorer in the 200 block of Machray Avenue. Two firearms were located in the vehicle and seized as evidence.
Shortly after midnight, officers observed the Ford Explorer commit a Highway Traffic Act infraction at Charles Street and Machray Avenue which resulted in a traffic stop in the rear lane at the above-mentioned address. As the vehicle came to a stop, the driver and two passengers fled on foot. Officers arrested a 46-year-old passenger outside the vehicle. He was found with almost $3,000 and 17 grams of Fentanyl on his person.
A second male passenger, also aged 46 years, and the 37-year-old woman driver were located at the intersection of Main Street and Cathedral Avenue where they were taken into custody without incident.
Officers searched the vehicle and seized the following:
A dismantled Remington 812 12-guage shotgun
A loaded Dan Wesson .357 revolver with a defaced serial number
A digital scale
Chantel Kim TRAVERSE (37)
is charged with multiple firearms-related offences and Fail to Comply with Condition of Undertaking x 2.
Ronald Jason LEATHWOOD (46)
is charged with firearms-related offences, drug trafficking, possession of proceeds of crime, and Fail to Comply with Release Order x 5.
Robert Allan THOMPSON (46)
is charged with similar firearms-related offences.
TRAVERSE, LEATHWOOD, and THOMPSON were detained in police custody awaiting further disposition.

title: Parking lot collision and assault leads to arrest and multiple charges: C26-2962
content:
On the afternoon of January 4, 2026, the Winnipeg Police Service responded to a disturbance in the 1400 block of Ellice Avenue stemming from motor vehicle collision in a parking lot. A 38-year-old man was arrested by responding West District officers and detained in custody.
At approximately 4:45 p.m., a 2013 Dodge Dart operated by the 38-year-old suspect, was observed driving erratically in the area of King Edward Street and Ness Avenue. Moments later, he was involved in a motor vehicle collision in a parking lot in the 1400 block of Ellice Avenue where he threatened the 52-year-old driver of the other involved vehicle. The incident was witnessed by bystanders who contacted police.
When a responding Community Support Unit (CSU) officer arrived, he observed the suspect assaulting a 23-year-old security guard who had intervened in the altercation. With assistance from responding West District General Patrol units and the security guard, the combative male was safely taken into custody. The CSU officer was physically assaulted during the arrest and sustained minor injuries which did not require medical attention. The security guard was uninjured.
Bobby Roger COUTU (38)
is charged with the following offences:
Assault a Peace Officer
Resist Peace Officer
Assault
Uttering Threats – Cause Death or Bodily Harm
Causing a Disturbance
Operation of a Conveyance While Impaired to Any Degree by BAC or Drug or Combination of Both
Fail or Refuse to Comply with Demand
Fail to Comply with Condition of Release Order
In addition, COUTU was issued a number of Highway Traffic Act Offence Notices including driving without a license and driving an unregistered vehicle. He was also arrested on the strength on two separate warrants of arrest for Fail to Attend Court and Fail to Comply with Release Order.
COUTU was detained in custody.

title: Officers intervene after observing unprovoked downtown assault – man in custody: C26-2812
content:
On January 4, 2026, patrolling Winnipeg Police Service officers arrested a 30-year-old man involved in the random, unprovoked assault of a woman in her 30’s in the 300 block of Portage Avenue.
At 1:30 p.m., West District General Patrol officers were travelling westbound on Portage Avenue near Donald Street when they observed a man physically assaulting a woman and knocking her to the ground. The officers quickly intervened, stopped the assault, and arrested the uncooperative suspect. During the arrest, one officer deployed a conductive energy weapon to safely take the suspect into custody. The woman suffered minor injuries and did not require medical attention.
The suspect and the victim were not previously known to one another and the assault appears to be random and unprovoked.
Jacob GEORGE (30)
has been charged with Assault and was detained in police custody awaiting further disposition.

title: Update: Investigators identify and arrest suspect in pellet gun shooting of transit operator: C25-256607
content:
On October 27, 2025, a Winnipeg Transit operator was assaulted shot in the hand with what is believed to be a pellet gun during a dispute with a fare. The incident was assigned to the Major Crimes Unit and the investigation continued. As a result of the investigation, a suspect was identified.
On January 4, 2026, a
14-year-old boy
was arrested at his residence in East Kildonan, and is facing the following charges:
Assault with a Weapon
Fail to Comply with Condition of Undertaking x 2
Mischief Under $5,000/Obstruct in Enjoyment
He was detained in custody.
As previously released:
On October 27, 2025 at 2:11 p.m., East District General Patrol officers responded to the intersection of Gateway Road and Springfield Road for the report of a youth that produced what is believed to be a pellet gun and shot a transit operator in the hand following a dispute. The operator received minor injuries and was transported to hospital in stable condition.
With the assistance of the Tactical Support Team and K9, officers searched the area for the youth, however, the youth had fled prior to police arrival.
The major Crimes Unit has assumed the investigation.

title: Shots fired in North End neighbourhood leads to multiple arrests - firearm, drugs seized: C26-1664
content:
On January 3, 2026, members of the Winnipeg Police Service responded to the 300 block of Manitoba Avenue for the report of shots fired outside of a residence. Officers arrested seven individuals into custody and seized a 9mm handgun, a quantity of illicit drugs, and $925 as evidence.
The investigation revealed that at approximately 2:40 a.m., a 38-year-old man and a 20-year-old woman became involved in a heated verbal argument inside a residence in the above-mentioned block. The argument escalated when the man physically assaulted the woman, causing minor injuries. Shortly after, while armed with a handgun, he exited the building, and recklessly discharged the firearm, striking a neighbouring residence. No one inside the neighbouring residence reported any injuries as a result of the firearm discharge.
Attending North District General Patrol officers, assisted by members of the K9 Unit and General Patrol officers from the Central and East Districts, located the 38-year-old man and the 20-year-old woman involved along with five additional people inside the residence where the assault had originated. All were arrested without incident.
During the subsequent execution of a search warrant for the residence, officers located and seized the following property:
A 9mm Roebuck handgun with a magazine containing 9mm ammunition
Approximately 3.6 Ounces of Fentanyl (Estimated Street Value: $5,400)
Approximately 3.9 Ounces of Methamphetamine (Estimated Street Value: $1,300)
Alexander Paul DOYLE (38)
has been charged with multiple firearms-related and drug trafficking-related offences, Assault, and Proceeds of Crime under $5,000. He was detained in custody.
Tyesha Sampaio LOBO (28), and
Travis Adam CHARTRAND (42)
were charged with similar firearms-related and drug-trafficking offences and were also detained in custody.
Two men in their 50’s
and
two women in their 20’s
face similar charges and were released on either Appearance Notices or Undertakings.

title: Man arrested in possession of loaded handgun and prohibited magazine following attempted assault on taxi driver: C26-2518
content:
On January 4, 2026, a 48-year-old man was detained following an attempted assault on a taxi driver in the William Whyte area. Officers subsequently arrested the man after locating a loaded handgun and a prohibited 13-round magazine on his person.
At approximately 1:40 a.m., an assault on a taxi driver was developing in the area of Burrows Avenue and Powers Street. The taxi driver observed a marked police cruiser and activated their emergency strobe light, grabbing the attention of the North District General Patrol officers and prompting the man to disengage.
Officers made a U-turn to investigate and observed the taxi pulled over in the 200 block of Powers Street and the suspect walking away. Officers spoke with the driver, who reported the man walking away had attempted to assault him. He was not injured as a result of the incident.
Officers detained the man in the 200 block of Powers Street, where he was found to be in possession of a loaded Springfield Hellcat 9x19 handgun with a prohibited 13 round magazine.
Robert Louis PARISIAN (48)
has been charged with:
Possession of Firearm, Restricted/Prohibited Weapon, Firearm Part or Ammunition Contrary to Prohibition Order
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Weapon Knowing its Possession is Unauthorized
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Firearm with Ammunition
Carrying Concealed Weapon Prohibited Device or Ammunition
PARISIAN was detained in custody.

title: Two arrested after convenience store clerk assaulted with a weapon: C26-2238
content:
On January 3, 2026 a man and a woman assaulted a convenience store employee with a weapon in the 400 block of Talbot Avenue. The clerk received minor injuries from the assault and did not require medical attention.
At approximately 7:12 p.m., a 37-year-old male and a 40-year-old female became involved in a dispute with a store clerk at the above-mentioned convenience store. During the dispute, the clerk was assaulted with various items obtained from within the store. The incident was interrupted by a person who entered the store during the assault, and police were contacted. The suspects left before police arrived.
East District General Patrol officers attended and reviewed security footage of the incident. While officers were speaking with the store clerk, the two suspects returned to the store, attempted to make a false claim that they had been assaulted by the employee, and were subsequently arrested.
Nico Randy SYLVESTRE (37)
has been charged with Assault with a Weapon. He was detained in custody.
A 40-year-old woman
is facing a charge of Assault with a Weapon. She was released on an Undertaking.

title: Man arrested after a fast food robbery: C26-488
content:
On January 1, 2026, around 2:45 p.m., officers from West District with the assistance of the Tactical Support Team, responded to a suspect boarding a transit bus following a commercial robbery reported moments earlier.
A man entered a fast-food restaurant in the 1500 block of Portage Avenue and demanded  money from the front till and threatened to shoot the employees.
The three employees ran to safety and the suspect circled around the counter and unsuccessfully attempted to open the cash register. He then entered the kitchen, and stole hamburgers and fries that were still cooking in frying pans. He exited the restaurant and boarded a transit bus where he proceeded to eat the food and tried to fight people on the bus. Nobody reported any assaults.
The bus had not travelled far, when it stopped and the suspect was taken into police custody. He was in possession of a stolen wallet.
Jonathan FONTAINE (29), was charged with the following offences:
Robbery
Possession of Property Obtained by Crime Under $5000
He was detained in custody.

title: Officers threatened and assaulted during shoplifting arrest: C25-313840
content:
On December 30, 2025, around 6:30 p.m., members of the Foot Patrol Unit were providing community engagement in the Central District. While at a store in the 300 block of Portage Avenue, they were alerted to someone attempting to leave the store without paying for merchandise.
The suspect was placed under arrest and he verbally threatened to harm one of the officers. An additional unit attended for transport purposes.
As the man was being placed into the police cruiser car he began to fight and one of the officers was kicked in the head. The officer did not require medical attention at the time.
A
37-year-old man
is facing the following charges:
Assault Peace Officer
Uttering Threats - Cause Death or Bodily Harm
Theft Under $5000
He was detained in custody.

title: Chief Peguis Street Racing and Just Slow Down Campaign
content:
Chief Peguis Street Racing – Multiple Offence Notices Issued: C26-114396
On May 16, 2026, at approximately 12:54 a.m., Air1 observed two vehicles travelling at excessive speeds and appearing to race along Chief Peguis Trail. One of the vehicles was estimated to be travelling in excess of 200 km/hr. and the incident was captured on video.
Air1 maintained observation of both vehicles and tracked them to a residence, where they were parked. Ground units were directed to the location and both vehicles and their registered owners were subsequently identified.
Offence notices for Racing and Careless Driving were issued to the registered owners. Responsibility for the offences will be determined through the court process.
Multiple Spring Vehicle Collisions under investigation with speed and aggressive driving considered to be a factor – Just Slow Down
The Winnipeg Police remind motorists that speed limits are established to promote safety for all road users. Excessive speeding, aggressive driving and street racing significantly increase the risk of serious collisions and endanger motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users.
In 2025, Winnipeg Police Service officers issued more than 13,194 speeding-related violations.
While speeding may save only a small amount of travel time, it can greatly increase both the likelihood and severity of a collision. Compliance with posted speed limits is an important part of keeping Winnipeg's roadways safe.
As the summer driving season is here, police encourage all motorists to slow down, exercise patience and make safe driving choices to help prevent injuries and save lives.

title: Safeguarding our youth online: Winnipeg Police Service warns of growing threat of nihilistic violent extremism targeting children
content:
The Winnipeg Police Service is issuing a public safety advisory to raise awareness of an escalating threat targeting children and youth in online spaces. Officers have begun delivering public awareness presentations on this topic to health care professionals, first responders, educators and school support staff, community agencies, and the general public to help increase awareness and support early recognition of the warning signs.
Predators once had to enter public spaces to seek out potential victims, but with evolving technology and social platforms, those behaviours have increasingly moved into online environments. Today, offenders are actively infiltrating online platforms children use daily, including Roblox, Minecraft, Snapchat, Discord, Telegram, and Twitch, amongst others.
The Threat:
Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) networks — including organized groups such as The Com Network (764, MKY, O9A, amongst others), and the True Crime Community (TCC) are deliberately targeting vulnerable children and youth online. Their stated objective is not ideological change, but the destruction of society.
These predators comb through online platforms in search of children expressing vulnerability — including posts about body image, loneliness, family conflict, bullying, or struggles with mental health and neurodiversity. Predators exploit these voluntary online disclosures by fabricating shared experiences to build false trust, then systematically introduce victims to increasingly violent and disturbing material, including child sexual abuse material, animal torture, and gore, as part of a deliberate desensitization process.
Predators then move victims to private spaces where grooming escalates to blackmail. Victims, including children as young as pre-teen, are coerced into committing harmful acts against themselves, their siblings, or their pets, sometimes while being forced to livestream the abuse. Extortion is not used for financial gain. It is a tool used to extract more material and to ultimately push victims towards taking their own lives or the lives of another.
By the Numbers
According to CSIS (2025), 1 in 10 terrorism investigations in Canada now involves at least one minor. The United States has seen a 300% increase in these occurrences in the past 12 months alone, and the trend is not slowing.
Members, particularly younger ones, escalate behaviours not out of genuine ideological commitment, but in pursuit of online validation and recognition — with the perceived risk of law enforcement attention sometimes serving as a badge of honour rather than a deterrent.
What Parents and Caregivers Should Watch For:
Unexplained injuries, markings, or signs of self-mutilation
Sudden withdrawal from family or longtime friends
Secretive or distressed behaviour around device use
Exposure to disturbing content or unfamiliar online contacts
Changes in mood, language, or expressed worldview
A Coordinated Community Response
The Winnipeg Police Service is actively working alongside Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service, HSC Children's Hospital, Winnipeg schools, and Animal Services to ensure that all potential first-contact agencies are informed and equipped to identify and respond to these occurrences.
If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call 9-1-1.
If you have information about a child who may be targeted or victimized, or you believe you may be a victim, contact the Winnipeg Police Service at 204-986-6222, or report it to
Cybertip.ca
. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through Crime Stoppers at 204-786-8477 (TIPS), or online at
www.manitobacrimestoppers.com
.
For more information and resources, please visit
Safeguarding our Youth Online
on the Winnipeg Police Service website.

title: Police arrest and charge suspect in Ontario homicide and Winnipeg threat case
content:
Police have charged an individual following a homicide investigation in the Township of Greater Madawaska, Ontario, that uncovered a potential threat to a business in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
On Wednesday, May 6, 2026, just before 6:00 p.m. EST (5:00 p.m. CST), members from the Renfrew Detachment of the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) responded to a call for service on Lanark Road in the Township of Greater Madawaska, where one person was located deceased. The deceased was later identified as 61-year-old Geraldine FULCHER of Calabogie, Ontario. The death was deemed a homicide.
Further investigation revealed information indicating ties to a potential threat to a business in downtown Winnipeg. The suspect was believed to have made threats to target the business and its employees and expressed a willingness to engage in a violent confrontation with police.
On Tuesday, May 12, 2026, at approximately 1:10 p.m. CST (2:10 p.m. EST), the Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) received information from the OPP that the homicide suspect was believed to be in Winnipeg and possibly in possession of a firearm. The OPP provided a description of the suspect and their vehicle.
At approximately 1:50 p.m. CST (2:50 p.m. EST), WPS West District General Patrol officers located the suspect and the vehicle in the 3600 block of Portage Avenue. The suspect was taken into custody without incident. During the arrest, officers seized a shotgun, ammunition, additional weapons and three jerrycans of gasoline.
The WPS Major Crimes Unit (MCU) notified the OPP of the arrest and assumed carriage of the threat investigation. The OPP Criminal Investigation Branch (CIB) members attended WPS Headquarters and interviewed the suspect in connection with the homicide in Ontario.
The WPS charged Graham MLODOZENEC, 52 years old of Sudbury, Ontario, with the following
Criminal Code
(CC) offences:
Possession of a loaded prohibited or restricted firearm, s. 95(1)
Possession of a weapon, s. 88(1)
Uttering threats – cause death or bodily harm, s. 264.1(1)(a)
Uttering threats – damage property, s. 264.1(1)(b)
Unauthorized possession of a firearm in motor vehicle, s. 94(1)
Unauthorized possession of a firearm, s. 91(1)
Careless storage of firearm, ammunition, prohibited weapon or device, s. 86(2)
Possession of incendiary material, s. 82(1)
On Monday, June 15, 2026, the accused was transferred into OPP custody and was further charged with the following CC offences:
First degree murder, s. 235(1)
Attempt murder of persons, s. 239(1)
The accused remains in custody in Ontario and is scheduled to appear before the Ontario Court of Justice in Pembroke on Monday, June 22, 2026.
Police will not be releasing the name of the business in order to protect the privacy of the employees and the ongoing court proceedings.
The OPP has assumed carriage of the homicide and threat investigations, which remain ongoing by the Renfrew OPP Crime Unit, under the direction of the OPP CIB, in conjunction with the Office of the Chief Coroner and Ontario Forensic Pathology Service. Support was provided by Winnipeg Police Service West District General Patrol and Major Crimes Unit, the OPP East Region Regional Support Team, the OPP Forensic Interview Team, OPP Forensic Identification Services, the OPP Emergency Response Team and the OPP Underwater Search and Recovery Unit. The Manitoba Prosecutions Service also provided assistance in this investigation.
Investigators are urging anyone with information to contact the OPP at 1-888-310-1122. Should you wish to remain anonymous, contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-8477 (TIPS) or
ontariocrimestoppers.ca
.
QUOTE
"This investigation demonstrates the seriousness with which police respond to potential threats and the importance of strong cross-provincial collaboration. Through combined police efforts, an arrest has been made in Geraldine’s homicide and additional harm was prevented. We thank the public for their patience and the Winnipeg Police Service for their swift action."
Detective Inspector Jason Winser, OPP CIB
“This incident underscores the vital importance of inter-agency cooperation in maintaining public safety. The coordinated efforts of the Winnipeg Police Service and the Ontario Provincial Police enabled a rapid response resulting in the successful apprehension of a violent high-risk suspect and preventing further harm to the public
."
Inspector Cory Francis, Winnipeg Police Service CIB

title: Winnipeg Police Service Introduces Ceremonial Eagle Feather
content:
Starting this month, the Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) is honoured to offer members of the public, as well as WPS members, the option of affirming legal oaths using an Eagle Feather.
An Eagle Feather is a sacred item and, when held, a person is expected to speak with honesty, truth, and integrity. This option carries the same legal standing as swearing on a Bible or making an affirmation. For many, it also provides cultural meaning and personal comfort.
The Eagle Feathers will be available at all four district stations.
Image
Eight Eagle Feathers were provided to the Service with the guidance and support of Elder Mike Calder, in partnership with Manitoba Conservation. Prepared in accordance with traditional protocols, feathers have been beaded with the colours of the Medicine Wheel and the four Nations. The beadwork was completed by women participating in the Indigenous Traditional Program at the Behavioural Health Foundation.
The WPS is honoured to be able to provide this culturally meaningful option, and we do so with deep respect for Indigenous traditions and the communities we serve.
June marks Indigenous History Month in Canada as a time to share culture, stories, and to honour the history of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis peoples. Our Service honours this month by deepening our understanding of Indigenous cultures and taking meaningful steps toward inclusivity. This includes adopting important practices into our policies and procedures.
Building deeper ties is both a responsibility of our Service as well as a powerful step forward in being proud community partners. We thank all those involved in this process for their continued commitment to the important steps of reconciliation.

title: Winnipeg Police Service Launches Modernized Bicycle Patrol Program
content:
The Winnipeg Police Service has launched a modernized Bicycle Patrol Program, equipping trained officers with new e-bikes that will enhance proactive patrols, increase visibility and improve access to neighbourhoods, pathways, parks, public gathering spaces and special events throughout the city.
Twenty-five officers have completed specialized bicycle patrol training and will be deployed across all four districts using a combination of mountain bikes and 16 newly acquired e-bikes.
The program is designed to enhance public safety by providing officers with another operational tool to access locations that may be difficult to reach by traditional patrol vehicles while maintaining a highly visible police presence in the community.
"Bicycle patrols allow officers to engage directly with residents, business owners and visitors while responding quickly to emerging issues in areas where traditional patrol vehicles may be less effective," said Sergeant Kelsey Mahoney, Bicycle Patrol Program Coordinator.
Officers assigned to the program remain fully operational and may be deployed to support calls for service, proactive patrols, major events, riverbank operations and other public safety initiatives throughout Winnipeg.
The Bicycle Patrol Program will operate between May and October.

title: Open Drug Enforcement Strategy Currently Underway
content:
The Winnipeg Police Service has recently seen a significant increase in open drug use and drug trafficking in public places in Winnipeg. This has led to overwhelming community concerns and complaints over public safety issues in neighbourhoods adversely affected by open drug use.
As a police service, we have a responsibility to address the harm being caused by the drug trade. We remain committed to targeting those who profit from addiction -- those who traffic illicit substances and contribute to the cycle of harm.
But we also know enforcement alone is not the solution.
Despite these efforts, drugs continue to reach our streets, and the impacts are visible. Open drug use is occurring in public spaces and it’s not something our community should have to accept. It affects safety, public health, and quality of life. And we must respond.
The Winnipeg Police Service has strategically increased presence in neighbourhoods most affected. These are data-driven geographic areas based on crime data, and mapping that will assist in identifying emerging trends and guide further enforcement and intervention efforts. These areas will continue to see an increased and visible police presence.
So far, the Winnipeg Police Service has achieved measurable results:
100 total interactions with individuals using drugs in public spaces
25 total arrests with two specifically related to drug possession or trafficking
3 individuals taken to Protective Care Centre
We are not criminalizing addiction. While the goal of the initiative is ultimately to deter and reduce open drug use and disrupt drug trafficking to make public spaces safer for all residents, individuals struggling with addictions will be offered connections to social supports and partner agencies.

title: Newly Designed Police Cruiser Showcases Indigenous Partnership
content:
The Winnipeg Police Service (WPS), in partnership with the Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs (AMC), is proud to present a newly designed WPS cruiser dedicated to improving relationships with our Indigenous community. The cruiser, which will be used solely by the Community Relations Division, was designed by Brian Hunter, a contemporary artist of Red River Metis descent, and member of the Winnipeg Police Service.
While the cruiser’s visual design honours Indigenous cultures, teachings, and traditions, its purpose reaches far beyond its appearance. This cruiser represents a meaningful step forward in building trust, strengthening relationships, and acknowledging the history, resilience, and contributions of Indigenous Peoples in our community. It serves as a reminder that policing is not only about public safety, but also about listening, learning, and working together in a spirit of mutual respect.
This initiative was made possible through the guidance and partnership of the Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs, whose leadership and collaboration were integral to the project’s development. Their involvement ensured the design and messaging are rooted in authenticity and cultural understanding.
Together, WPS and Indigenous partners are demonstrating a shared vision of Reconciliation in action, one that moves beyond words and symbolism to foster genuine connection, dialogue, and accountability. This cruiser embodies a collective commitment to ongoing partnership, community engagement, and a future where Indigenous voices continue to help shape policing in Winnipeg.
Members of the public will be able to request its appearance at different events, such as pow wows, parades, or other celebrations.

84-year-old male pedestrian
with serious injuries after being struck by a passenger vehicle. He was transported to the hospital in unstable condition, where he later succumbed to his injuries.

86-year-old male driver

title: Youth injured by moving train in Weston neighbourhood: C26- 161738
content:
On July 3, 2026, around 8:45 p.m., the Winnipeg Police Service responded to the report of a youth who had been injured by a moving train on the tracks in the 1300 block of Winnipeg Avenue West.
The Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service (WFPS), also on scene, transported the youth to hospital in unstable condition; later upgraded to stable.
The public is reminded to exercise extreme caution when in and around active rail lines. Never attempt to climb on rail equipment or approach a moving train under any circumstances.
More rail safety information is available here
.

title: Man charged with 22 offences, after pointing loaded firearm at officers: C26-160958
content:
On July 3, 2026, just after 8:00 a.m., officers from North District were patrolling in a marked cruiser car, when they observed a man riding an electric bicycle along the sidewalk of McGregor Street. Contrary to the Highway Traffic Act, police attempted a traffic stop as he rode northbound McGregor. He failed to stop and continued riding, turning east on Manitoba Avenue. He eventually stopped in the 500 block of Manitoba Avenue.
Police identified the man, and determined he was breaching conditions of the electronic monitoring program (ankle monitor). While taking him into custody, police felt an unidentified object concealed on his body. The man resisted, wiggling out of his sweater and ran from police.
As officers ran after him, the accused pointed an object at police, (later confirmed to be a loaded firearm).
He was tackled to the ground and the firearm slid across the street. The accused was telling people in the area to retrieve it.
He was secured in handcuffs and police seized the weapon – a sawed-off .22 calibre improvised gun with a live round.
Glen Edward LUSSIER (35), was charged with 22 offences, including:
Assault Peace Officer with Weapon x 2
15 Firearms-related offences
Fail to Comply with Probation Order x 5
He was detained in custody.

title: Preschool-aged child sustains serious injuries, 39-year-old charged: R26-38054
content:
On July 6, 2026, the Winnipeg Police Service Child Abuse Unit was contacted after a preschool-aged child was transported by ambulance and admitted for treatment of serious injuries.
Investigators learned that earlier that day, the child was being cared for by a 39-year-old man at a residence in the 300 block of Thames Avenue when the injuries occurred. The man contacted emergency services, and Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service attended and transported the child to the hospital.
On July 7, 2026, at approximately 5:05 p.m., investigators located the 39-year-old man in the 300 block of Thames Avenue, where he was taken into custody.
The
39-year-old
has been charged with Aggravated Assault and was detained in custody.

title: Man in custody following multiple robberies involving an edged weapon: C26-149892
content:
On June 22, 2026, between approximately 12:30 p.m. and 12:45 p.m., the Winnipeg Police Service responded to a series of robberies involving an armed suspect. Police located the suspect a short time later and took him into custody.
At approximately 12:30 p.m., an adult male attended a grocery store in the 200 block of Salter Street and made known his intent to rob the business. The suspect assaulted one employee with a baton and attempted to assault another with an edged weapon. The employees and two security guards sought refuge in a room, at which time the suspect barricaded the front door to prevent them from leaving. The suspect eventually fled the store, and police were contacted. No serious injuries were reported.
Shortly after, the suspect approached two men working in the area of Magnus Avenue and Salter Street and attempted to rob them. They were able to escape without injury and contacted police.
The suspect then approached a 19-year-old man near the intersection of Magnus Avenue and Salter Street, assaulted him, and attempted to rob him. The victim was able to escape without injury and contacted police.
North District General Patrol officers attended the area and located the suspect on Salter Street near Magnus Avenue. Upon seeing police, he fled on foot but was taken into custody a short time later. Officers seized two weapons during the arrest.
Julius Joseph MCKAY (29)
has been charged with:
CC 343-344(1)(b) Robbery x6
CC 279(2) Forcible Confinement x3
CC 88 Possession of a Weapon x2
CC 90(1) Carrying Concealed Weapon Prohibited Device or Ammunition x2
MCKAY was detained in custody.

title: St. Vital Walmart arson results in multi-million-dollar property damage - suspect in custody: C26-164701/C26-166417
content:
A 47-year-old man is in custody after a fire was deliberately set at the St. Vital Walmart located at 1255 St. Mary’s Road on July 6, 2026.
Shortly before 7:00 p.m., the suspect attended the bedding section of the store and proceeded to set fire to bedding products. The fire quickly spread and resulted in thick black smoke permeating through the store. While the fire spread, the suspect attended an attached fast-food restaurant, helped himself to a beverage from the soft drink machine, and sat down at one of the tables. Within moments, the 150-200 patrons and staff were evacuated from the building.
Members of the WFPS attended and successfully knocked down the fire. Property damage is estimated at over ten million dollars.
The Major Crimes Unit assumed the investigation and soon identified the suspect as
Ronald Marmito AMIGO (47).
On July 9, 2026, members of the Bail Compliance Unit located and arrested AMIGO in the 300 block of Furby Street without incident. A small amount of methamphetamine and a lighter were located on his person and seized as evidence.
AMIGO is charged with the following offences:
Arson with Disregard for Human Life
Arson Causing Damage to Property
Possession of Incendiary Material
Fail to Comply with Probation Order x 2
Theft Under $5,000
Possession of a Controlled Substance - Methamphetamine
AMIGO was detained in police custody awaiting further disposition.

title: Two women charged after serious assault involving baseball bat: C26-159428
content:
Two women are in custody after two women were injured during a serious assault involving a weapon at a residence in the West End on July 1, 2026. Both victims were transported to hospital in critical condition and have since been upgraded to critical but stable condition.
On July 1, 2026, at approximately 4:20 p.m., Winnipeg Police responded to a residence in the 1100 block of Sherburn Street after receiving a report of two injured women inside. West and East District General Patrol officers attended and located a
25-year-old woman and 32-year-old woman
suffering from serious injuries consistent with being assaulted with a weapon. Officers provided first aid until members of the Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service arrived.
Officers learned that the two victims were at the residence with a
26-year-old woman and a 30-year-old woman, both of whom were known to them. At one point, an argument occurred and escalated to the point where the victims were assaulted with a baseball bat. Following the assault, one of the suspects photographed the injured victims and sent the images to other individuals. Police were subsequently contacted.
One of the victims was able to provide officers with information regarding the identities of the two suspects.
Between 5:42 p.m. and 6:12 p.m., both suspects were located and taken into custody. Officers also seized a baseball bat from the residence.
Miranda CROW (26)
has been charged with:
Aggravated Assault x2
Fail to Comply with Condition of Release Order x2
Fail to Comply with Probation Order
CROW was detained in custody.
Chantel Margaret OWEN (30)
has been charged with:
Aggravated Assault x2
Possession of a Weapon
OWEN was detained in custody

winnipegcrimestoppers.org
.

title: Central Community Support Unit arrests three suspects in relation to Downtown drug trafficking investigation: R26-34526
content:
On July 11, 2026, as a result of a search warrant executed at a residence in the 600 block of Elgin Avenue, members of the Winnipeg Police Service arrested two men and a woman seizing illicit drugs, weapons, a firearm, and cash in the process.
In June of 2026, members of the Central Division’s Community Support Unit began an investigation regarding drug trafficking in Winnipeg’s Central Downtown area. During the investigation, the above-mentioned address and a 30-year-old male suspect were identified. Officers obtained a search warrant for the involved residence.
On July 11, with assistance from the East District Community Support Unit, Central District General Patrol, and the Tactical Support Team, Central Community Support Unit members executed a search warrant at the residence. The 30-year-old male suspect, along with a 69-year-old-male and a 26-year-old female were found in the residence and placed under arrest.
As a result of the search warrant, officers seized the following property:
Beretta .40 calibre handgun with obliterated serial number
Various ammunition
Machete
Bear spray canister
40 individually packaged bags of crack cocaine totaling 12.6 g (Estimated Street Value: $800)
2.8 g of powder cocaine (Estimated Street Value: $300)
$565 CDN currency
Dillon Riley BARKER (30)
and
Savannah Taylor SANDERSON (26)
are charged with the following offences:
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Firearm with Ammunition
Possession of a Firearm Knowing Serial Number has been tampered with
Possession of a Firearm Knowing its Possession is Unauthorized
Store Firearm or Restricted Weapon contrary to Regulations
Possession of Firearm, Restricted/Prohibited Weapon, Firearm Part or Ammunition Contrary to Prohibition Order x 2
Possession of a Weapon x 2
Possession of a Scheduled Substance for the Purpose of Trafficking - Cocaine
Possession of Proceeds of Property Obtained by Crime Under $5,000
Both were detained in custody.
The
69-year-old male
faces similar, firearm, weapon, and drug trafficking-related charges and was released on an Undertaking to appear in court at a later date.
The WPS Community Support Units work to reduce and prevent criminal activity that affects our local neighbourhoods. By addressing concerns from citizens and businesses, Community Support Unit officers form relationships and aim to build safer communities through proactive action.

title: Kidnapping, armed robbery, and extortion investigation results in three arrests: R24-49671
content:
Three men have been charged following a lengthy investigation into the kidnapping of a delivery driver who was held at gunpoint for several hours while suspects stole approximately $25,000 worth of merchandise from a business and storage facility.
On the evening of October 11, 2024, a
22-year-old man
was delivering merchandise to a business in the 300 block of Nairn Avenue when he was confronted by a suspect armed with a firearm. The suspect held the firearm to the victim's head and forced him into the rear of an enclosed trailer. The victim's cellular phone and store merchandise were stolen.
The victim was then held at gunpoint under threats of harm to him and his family while suspects transported him to a storage facility in the 1300 block of Notre Dame Avenue. Once there, the victim was forced to provide access codes to a storage unit. Suspects stole an additional approximately $25,000 worth of merchandise from the storage lockers and transported the property to various locations throughout the city while the victim remained confined.
The incident concluded when the victim was dropped off in the 300 block of Nairn Avenue, where the ordeal had begun. No physical injuries were reported.
The victim attended Winnipeg Police Service Headquarters and reported the incident. The Major Crimes Unit assumed the investigation and identified three suspects.
On December 20, 2024, Major Crimes Unit investigators, with the assistance of the Canine Unit (K9), Air1, and the Manitoba Integrated Violent Offender Apprehension Unit (MIVOAU), located a
then 41-year-old suspect
in the 900 block of Sherbrook Street and took him into custody. During the arrest, Air1 flight crew observed him discard a firearm into a garbage bin. The firearm was recovered and determined to have been stolen. Officers also seized approximately 50 cartons of unstamped cigarettes.
On July 31, 2025, Major Crimes Unit investigators, with the assistance of MIVOAU, located a
34-year-old
suspect in the area of McPhillips Street and Notre Dame Avenue and took him into custody. During the arrest, investigators seized a knife, approximately five grams of methamphetamine, and 2.5 grams of cocaine with an estimated value of $200.
On July 6, 2026, the Treaty Three Police Service located a
35-year-old suspect
in Sabaskong, Ontario. He was transported to the Falcon Lake area, where he was turned over to MIVOAU members, returned to Winnipeg, and subsequently turned over to Major Crimes Unit investigators.
Jonathon RANGER (43)
has been charged with:
Kidnapping
Armed Robbery using a Restricted Firearm or Prohibited Firearm
Extortion Using a Restricted Firearm or Prohibited Firearm
Uttering Threats - Cause Death or Bodily Harm
Break Enter & Theft – Place
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Weapon Knowing its Possession is Unauthorized
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Firearm with Ammunition
Store Firearm or Restricted Weapon Contrary to Regs
Possession of Firearm, Restricted/Prohibited Weapon, Firearm Part or Ammunition Contrary to Prohibition Order x5
Fail to Comply with Condition of Undertaking
Possession of Contraband Cigarettes etc. not Manitoba Marked
RANGER was detailed in custody.
Tyson Shane DANIELS (34)
has been charged with:
Kidnapping
Armed Robbery using a Firearm
Extortion
Uttering Threats - Cause Death or Bodily Harm
Use of Imitation Firearm During Commission of an Indictable Offence
Warrant – Carrying Concealed Weapon Prohibited Device or Ammunition
Warrant – Fail to Comply with Condition of Release Order x2
Possession of Scheduled Substance – Methamphetamine
Possession of Scheduled Substance – Cocaine
Possession of Scheduled Substance – COCAINE
Fail to Comply with Condition of Release Order
Break Enter & Theft – Place
DANIELS was detained in custody.
Terrence Joel MCIVOR (35)
has been charged with:
Kidnapping

title: IIU Investigation – Officer involved shooting: C26-171585
content:
On July 13, 2026 at approximately 8:42 p.m., the Winnipeg Police Service received a family trouble call at a residence on Avon Gate in Lindenwoods. A man called about his adult brother’s concerning behaviour. The caller had been locked out of their house by his brother.
At 9:58 p.m., the man called police again as he was still locked out of the house and his brother was now screaming at him through a window.
At 10:23 p.m., a West District General Patrol Unit arrived onscene in a marked cruiser car.
At 10:35 p.m., the police were confronted by the man who exited the home while armed with an edged weapon. A use of force encounter occurred and a police service firearm was discharged, and the man was critically injured.
Officers immediately provided emergency medical care to the man, and a neighbour also rushed over to assist.
The
42-year-old man
was transported to hospital in critical condition and succumbed to his injuries.
The Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) has assumed responsibility for the investigation. Please direct any follow-up inquiries to the IIU.

title: Impaired driver causes extensive property damage in downtown collision: C26-177034
content:
A
49-year-old man
is facing an impaired driving charge after losing control of a vehicle and causing extensive property damage in downtown Winnipeg.
On July 19, 2026, at approximately 9:26 a.m., Central District General Patrol officers attended to the area of Balmoral Street and Sargent Avenue following reports of a motor vehicle collision involving a downed hydro line and damage to a bus shelter and City of Winnipeg traffic signal box.
Officers learned that a 2005 Ford Mustang, being operated by a 49-year-old man, was travelling eastbound on Sargent Avenue at a high rate of speed when it attempted to turn onto Balmoral Street and lost control. The vehicle collided with a bus shelter and a Manitoba Hydro pole before continuing into a traffic signal box. The vehicle ultimately came to rest with its front wheels suspended off the ground. No injuries were reported.
After speaking with the driver, officers determined his ability to operate a motor vehicle was impaired by alcohol, and he was taken into custody.
The 49-year-old man is facing a charge of Operation of a Conveyance While Impaired to Any Degree by BAC or Drug or a Combination of Both. He was released on an Appearance Notice.

title: Missing cat investigation leads to extortion charge: C26-172416
content:
A
72-year-old man
is facing extortion and theft-related charges after demanding money in exchange for the return of a stolen cat in Winnipeg's North End.
On July 14, 2026, a
44-year-old woman
reported that her cat had gone missing from her residence in the 200 block of Manitoba Avenue. She told police she suspected a neighbouring resident was involved. The neighbour later admitted to the victim that he was in possession of the cat and delivered a letter demanding money in exchange for its return. This information was relayed to police.
On July 16, North District General Patrol officers attended the neighbouring residence and located the cat inside unharmed. The cat was subsequently returned to the victim.
A 72-year-old man
is facing Extortion and Theft Under $5,000 charges. He was released on an Undertaking.

title: Four hospitalized following speed-related multi-vehicle collision: C26-175445
content:
On July 17, 2026, officers of the Winnipeg Police Service responded to a serious collision involving three vehicles and a motorcycle. Four adults required transportation to hospital with serious and critical injuries.
At 5:30 p.m., North District officers responded and attended to the vicinity of Main Street and Jarvis Avenue where a passing Central Processing Unit Officer was providing emergency first aid to the motorcycle operator. Members of the Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service attended and took over medical support for the multiple injured parties, transporting three patients in unstable condition and one in critical condition. All were stabilized in hospital, however, the motorcycle operator suffered potentially life-altering injuries.
The preliminary investigation indicated that a
2014 BMW 328i XDrive
with two occupants, and a
2022 Indian Challenger
motorcycle with an operator and one passenger, were travelling southbound alongside one another at a high rate of speed, when a Ford Escape proceeded into the path of the speeding vehicles. The Ford clipped the rear of the BMW causing it to collide with a nearby building on the west side of Main while the Indian motorcycle struck the rear of the Escape resulting in both riders being thrown from the motorcycle. The BMW also struck a second SUV with two occupants, before ultimately coming to a stop.
Four involved persons were transported to hospital with various injuries ranging from minor to potentially life-altering. The remaining involved parties were treated at the scene.
Speed is believed to be the primary factor leading to the collisions.
The Winnipeg Police remind motorists that speed limits are established to promote safety for all road users. Excessive
speeding, aggressive driving and street racing significantly increase the risk of serious collisions and endanger motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users.
The Traffic Division is continuing with the investigation.
Anyone with information, or who may have dashcam, security, or cell phone video from around the time of the incident, is asked to contact the Traffic Division at
204-986-7085 or anonymously through Crime Stoppers 204-786-TIPS or
winnipegcrimestoppers.org
.

title: Youth charged after animal cruelty incident in Centennial neighbourhood: C26-178513
content:

title: Man arrested after highspeed road racing along Disraeli into the Elmwood neighbourhood : C26-183591

title: 2026 Winnipeg Police Service Public Opinion Survey
content:
Every two years, the Winnipeg Police Service, in conjunction with the Winnipeg Police Board, contracts out a public opinion telephone survey to an independent agency. The anonymous survey asks citizens about their view of the Service and their opinions about crime and public safety in our city. During the week of July 27, 2026, Prairie Research Associates (a local independent market research firm) will randomly call individuals in all areas of the City of Winnipeg. The survey requires approximately 15 minutes to complete.
Once completed, the survey results will be made public and discussed at a public Winnipeg Police Board meeting and posted on the
Winnipeg Police Service
and
Winnipeg Police Board
websites.
Citizens can be assured the survey is legitimate if they receive a call from Prairie Research Associates between these dates.
If you are 18 and older, please consider participating in this valuable opinion survey. Your feedback is how change begins.
The Winnipeg Police Service thanks all residents who take the time to participate in the survey.

title: An armed & barricaded arson, resulted in tenants being evacuated from an apartment in the 600 block of Sherbrook Street: C26-182410
content:
On July 24, 2026, around 10:15 p.m., on-site security (a man-victim 2) was at an apartment block in the 600 block of Sherbrook Street when he was approached by a woman (victim 1) who indicated she had been assaulted by an adult family member inside a suite. She requested assistance in retrieving her property from the suite. When the security member attended the suite, he was confronted by the accused, who was armed with a knife. He held the knife to the security person’s throat, and threatened to kill him.
The security member managed to run out and called 911, while the armed man remained inside the suite.
Officers from Central District, with the assistance of the Tactical Support Team (TST), K9 and the Drone Unit attended and determined the situation had transitioned into an armed and barricaded incident.
The accused proceeded to set a fire inside the suite and the building quickly became smoke filled. Approximately two dozen tenants (including children) were safely evacuated by officers. No injuries were reported.
Members from TST gained access to the suite where the accused eventually dropped the weapon and TST entered through the active fire, removing the accused from the suite into the hallway.
While taking him into custody, the accused was combative and a use of force encounter occurred. He was placed in handcuffs and extracted from the burning building.
The accused was transported to hospital and treated for minor injuries.
The original female victim declined medical attention at the time.
One of the ten officers who entered the building was assessed by members of the Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service for smoke inhalation and did not require hospitalization.
Timothy Bret McKAY (24)
is charged with the following offences:
Arson with Disregard for Human Life
Assault with a Weapon
Assault
Resist Peace Officer
McKAY was detained in custody.

title: Man Issued with Multiple Provincial Offence Notices Related to Animal Welfare: C26-186572
content:
A
67-year-old man
received multiple provincial offence notices after the Winnipeg Police Service investigated a report of a large German Shepherd left unattended in a vehicle in a grocery parking lot in the 600 block of Osborne Street.
On July 29, 2026, at 1:00 p.m., West District General Patrol officers responded to a grocery store parking lot in the above-mentioned block, where they learned that the involved vehicle had already left.
Through their investigation, officers learned that at approximately 1:00 p.m., a man attended the above-mentioned parking lot, parked, and entered the store, leaving his dog inside the vehicle. Several concerned bystanders provided the thirsty, distressed dog with cold water through a slightly open window. At one point, the driver confronted the bystanders and returned to the store to shop. Bystanders continued to provide the dog water while its owner continued with his shopping.
When the owner returned to his vehicle, he continued to be belligerent with bystanders before striking one with his vehicle, reversing into a parked pick-up truck and fleeing the area at a high rate of speed.
Officers identified the driver and subsequently attended a residence in the Lord Roberts neighbourhood where they located the German Sheppard tied in the backyard. Officers were met by the belligerent 67-year-old male.
The male was provided with the following Provincial Offence Notices and Serious Offence Notice:
Highway Traffic Act
Driver Carelessly
Parking where Prohibited
Fail to Exchange Particulars
Animal Care Act
Inflict suffering, anxiety, distress upon an animal
Fail to ensure adequate source of food or water for an animal
Fail to provide an animal with reasonable protection from injurious heat or cold

: the outside temperature on this date was approximately 30° Celsius with a Humidex of 43° Celsius.

title: Winnipeg Police Arrest Man Wanted on Canada-Wide Warrant, Seize Loaded Handgun: C26-186924
content:
On July 29, 2026, members of the Winnipeg Police Service arrested a male wanted on a Canada-wide warrant, after observing him operating an electric scooter erratically in the city’s North End. A loaded firearm was seized during the arrest.
Shortly before 8:00 p.m., North District General Patrol officers observed
22-year-old Owen Lucas PISTUN
operating an electronic scooter travelling southbound on Salter Street and between Salter and Redwood Avenues. PISTUN could be seen weaving in and out of lanes causing traffic to slow down and creating a traffic hazard.
As officers attempted a traffic stop in the 200 block of Salter Street, PISTUN fled on foot but was quickly apprehended by police. During the arrest, PISTUN was observed reaching into a body worn satchel prompting the deployment of a conducted energy weapon (Taser) in order to safely take PISTUN into custody.
Property Seized
As a result of a subsequent search of PISTUN, the following property was seized by officers:
Loaded Glock 26 9mm handgun with a 15-round overcapacity magazine with 12 rounds (located in satchel)
4.5 Percocet pills
Approximately $1,300 CDN currency
PISTUN was also arrested on two warrants of arrest, one for being unlawfully-at-large and the other being a Canada-wide parole revocation warrant.
Charges
PISTUN is charged with the following offences:
Possession of a Prohibited or Restricted Firearm with Ammunition
Possession of a Firearm Knowing its Possession is Unauthorized
Possession of a Prohibited Device or Ammunition Knowing its Possession is Unauthorized
Carrying Concealed Weapon Prohibited Device or Ammunition
Possession of Firearm, Restricted/Prohibited Weapon, Firearm Part or Ammunition Contrary to Prohibition Order (three counts)
Resist Peace Officer
Possession of a Scheduled Substance for the Purpose of Trafficking
Possession of Proceeds of Property Obtained by Crime Under $5,000
PISTUN was also issued a ticket under the Highway Traffic Act for careless driving.
PISTUN remains in custody.

title: Hate Crimes Unit Investigates Incident at Watt Street Islamic Centre: C26-187131
content:
The Winnipeg Police Service Hate Crimes Unit is investigating a suspected hate-motivated attack on the Rahma Islamic Centre located in the 500 block of Watt Street.
On July 29, 2026, at approximately 11:30 p.m., passing East District officers observed freshly broken windows at the mosque. Officers initiated an investigation and learned that a suspect vehicle had driven by, during which time, a firearm was potentially discharged in the direction of the mosque, which is believed to have caused damage to the windows, before fleeing southbound on Watt Street. Later, two suspects arrived on foot and caused additional damage by breaking additional windows with an unknown object. No injuries were reported.
Additionally, officers also learned that suspects had attended earlier in the evening and shouted racist comments towards patrons.
The WPS is treating the incident as a potential hate-motivated crime involving both property damage and the reported discharge of a firearm at a mosque.
In light of this incident, the Winnipeg Police Service intends to increase its presence and patrols in and around the Rahma Islamic Centre and other area mosques.
The Hate Crimes Unit continues to investigate the incident.
Anyone with information, video, including dash cam video, is asked to contact the Major Crimes Unit at 204-986-6219 or anonymously at Crime Stoppers 204-786-TIPS or
winnipegcrimestoppers.org
Reports regarding hate motivated crime (excluding graffiti) can be made in person, by calling non-emergency at 204-986-2222, on through
online
reporting.

title: Homicide Investigation, Suspect in Custody: C26-187857
content:
A 23-year-old woman has been charged with Second Degree Murder following a fatal stabbing in downtown Winnipeg.
On July 28, 2026, at approximately 2:45 p.m., Winnipeg Police Service officers responded to the 300 block of Portage Avenue after receiving a report that a woman had been stabbed.
Attending Central District General Patrol officers located an adult female suffering from severe, life-threatening injuries. She was transported to hospital in critical condition but later died from her injuries. The suspect had fled the area before police arrived.
The deceased has been identified as
58-year-old Helen Annie SPENCE, a member of Grand Rapids First Nation, who had been residing in Winnipeg.
Following an investigation by the Homicide Unit,
Shante Trinity PAUL
,, was identified as the suspect.
PAUL was arrested without incident during the early morning hours of July 29 and has been charged with Second Degree Murder.
She remains in custody.

title: Winnipeg Police Arrest Man in RCMP Drug Trafficking Investigation: C26-185708

title: IIU Investigation – Officer Involved Shooting: C26-191138
content:
On August 3, 2026, at approximately 2:27 a.m., a Winnipeg Police Service North District Unit officer was in the vicinity of Aikins Street and College Avenue when he heard the sound of multiple gunshots nearby.
The officer immediately attended to the location of the gunshots to investigate and was confronted by a woman and a 16-year-old youth. A use of force encounter occurred, a police service firearm was discharged, and the woman was injured.
Emergency medical care was immediately provided to the 18-year-old woman, and she was transported to hospital in unstable condition, later upgraded to stable condition.
A firearm was recovered from the suspects.
Investigators have determined that the adult female and 16-year-old youth are linked to a shooting that occurred outside a residence in the 300 block of College Avenue at approximately 2:27 a.m. The
16-year-old youth
has been arrested.
As this matter is deemed a serious incident pursuant to
The Police Services Act, the Civilian Director of the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) was notified.
The Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) has assumed responsibility for the investigation. Please direct any follow-up inquiries to the IIU.

title: Road rage incident leads to the arrest of a man: C26-161186
content:
On August 3, 2026, just before 6:00 a.m., West District General Patrol officers responded to the area of St James Street and Ness Avenue for the report of a gun.
Officers arrived on scene and determined through investigation that a road rage incident had taken place between two men. The incident began when a man pulled his vehicle next to the one driven by the 53-year-old victim and began a verbal argument over the victim’s manner of driving. This escalated to the point where the suspect brandished a black handgun. The victim fled in his vehicle, but the suspect followed him a short distance and forced the victim to stop his vehicle by pulling in front of him. The suspect got out of his vehicle while still brandishing the black handgun before getting back into his vehicle and fleeing the area when he saw the victim contacting police. The victim was not injured as a result of this incident.
Further investigation identified the suspect, and he was arrested just before 7:30 p.m. at a residence on Beachham Crescent.
A
29-year-old man
is facing a charge of Assault with a Weapon and was released on an Undertaking.

Image

title: Winnipeg Police Service to continue enforcement and engagement efforts in downtown Winnipeg
content:
Following consultation with community stakeholders, the Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) will restart enforcement and engagement efforts beginning Friday, August 7th, aimed at curbing open drug use and trafficking in areas where there have been ongoing concerns related to crime and social disorder.
Working alongside community and government partners, the WPS will engage with individuals, enforce applicable laws and bylaws, and help connect people to appropriate supports and resources.
As a direct result of conversations with community stakeholders, the WPS will utilize suggestions made to ensure a community-focused initiative:
An outreach-first approach
: The WPS will prioritize collaboration with community organizations. Outreach workers may attend alongside officers, lead initial engagement efforts, or provide follow-up support to help connect individuals with appropriate services.
Enhanced community communication:
A dedicated Community Coordinator from Ka Ni Kanichik has been identified as the primary liaison between the WPS and community organizations, helping ensure concerns, information, and supports are shared effectively.
Stronger collaboration:
Community and policing partners will work together through a coordinated response to better address community concerns and connect people with appropriate supports.
10-Day initiative results
In the four weeks preceding the launch of the initiative, hotspots identified within the project boundaries experienced four consecutive weeks of increasing crime. Between June 24 - July 3, the WPS increased presence in these neighbourhoods affected by open drug use and social disorder.
During this 10-day period, the WPS engaged in the following activities:
Total Events (Officer Generated and related Calls for Service) – 1,099
Total Arrests – 106
93 Warrants and/or Breaches
3 Possession of a Scheduled Substance for the Purpose of Trafficking
5 Possession of a Scheduled Substance
Total number of persons transported to Protective Care Centre – 7
During this 10-day period, the WPS observed the following impacts:
Property crime incidents decreased 10.5% compared to the same period in 2025
Violent crime incidents decreased 16.5% compared to the same period in 2025
Emergency calls for service (Priority 0-2) decreased 6% compared to the same period in 2025
This initiative will continue to identify specific geographic areas in and around downtown Winnipeg. These locations have been selected based on a combination of WPS crime data, Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service data, and public tips and concern. Residents can expect to see a visible police presence in these areas meant to deter and suppress open drug use, intercept trafficking networks, and promote community outreach.
This work relies on continued collaboration with community partners. The WPS thanks everyone who has been involved in consulting on this initiative to improve public safety for all Winnipeggers.

title: Major Crimes Unit investigates assault on transit operator: C26-192973
content:
A City of Winnipeg transit operator was assaulted with a weapon while operating a bus in the area of Isabel Street and William Avenue.
On August 5, 2026, at 1:18 a.m., North District General Patrol officers responded to a report of a stabbing involving a transit operator and rider. Officers learned that the rider became disruptive after being asked to pay the fare. Before the rider exited the bus, the driver was stabbed in the lower body with an unknown object.
The driver received minor injuries and was transport to hospital in stable condition.
The Major Crimes Unit has assumed responsibility for the investigation.
Anyone with information, or who may have dashcam, security, or cell phone video from around the time of the incident, is asked to contact the Major Crimes Unit at 204-986-6219 or anonymously at Crime Stoppers 204-786-TIPS or
winnipegcrimestoppers.org
.

title: Winnipeg Police Seize Contraband Tobacco from Sherbrook Street Residence: C26-192570
content:
On August 4, 2026, members of the Winnipeg Police Service arrested a
36-year-old male suspect
after seizing over 60 boxes of contraband tobacco from a residence in the 600 block of Sherbrook Street.
Shortly before 2:30 p.m., Central District General Patrol officers were investigating an unrelated incident at the above-mentioned address when they observed a large quantity of illegal tobacco products.
The investigation was subsequently taken over by the Property Crime Unit, which obtained a search warrant for the residence. While officers secured the suite pending the warrant, the suspect returned and was arrested without incident.
In the early morning hours of August 5, officers executed the search warrant and seized:
Nearly 3000 cigarette cartons (Estimated total of 600,000 individual cigarettes)
$1,500 CDN currency
The 36-year-old suspect faces charges of Possession of Property Obtained by Crime Under $5,000 and Trafficking in Contraband Tobacco.
He was released on an undertaking and is scheduled to appear in court at a later date.

title: IIU Investigation – Officer Involved Motor Vehicle Collision C26-195638
content:
On August 7, 2026, just before 9:00 p.m., Winnipeg Police Service North District officers were responding to a call for service, travelling westbound on Portage Avenue at Garry Street. The officers entered the intersection on a green light when their cruiser collided with a cyclist travelling northbound on Garry Street, knocking the female cyclist to the ground and injuring her.
Officers immediately stopped and provided emergency medical care to the 37-year-old cyclist. She was transported to hospital in stable condition.
As this matter is deemed a serious incident pursuant to
The Police Services Act, the Civilian Director of the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) was notified.
The Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba (IIU) has assumed responsibility for the investigation. Please direct any follow-up inquiries to the IIU.

title: Sex Crimes investigation leads to charges. One man arrested: C26-68868
content:

The survivor reported that he made acquaintance in July 2023 with another adult man on a social website, and they met in person on more than one occasion.
During one of the occasions, they met at a residence in the southwest area of the city. While at the residence, the survivor was provided an illicit drug and was sexually assaulted.

On August 10, 2026,

title: Traffic investigation of imitation police vehicle leads to fine: R26-46247
content:
On August 10, 2026, the Winnipeg Police Service’s Traffic Division began an investigation after receiving information of a video depicting a white Ford Explorer that was in the parking lot of a commercial business in the 1-99 block of Sage Creek Boulevard on August 9, 2026, with active flashing red and blue lights in its rear window.
The Traffic Unit continued the investigation, and the driver of the vehicle was identified.
Officers met with the 17-year-old driver who admitted placing temporary red and blue flashing lights on the rear window using suction cups as a dare from his friends.
A preliminary examination of the vehicle revealed it to be an ex-police unit that had been properly decommissioned with no lights or marking that would indicate it being in active service.
A vehicle inspection on the vehicle was conducted and the tint on the front driver and passenger side windows were found to be in violation of the Vehicle Equipment, Safety and Inspection Regulation (VESI). A re-inspection and VESI ticket were issued.
The 17-year-old youth was educated on the consequences of operating a vehicle marked with emergency lighting that actively portrays it as an active police service vehicle.
The Winnipeg Police Service takes the representation of police vehicles very seriously. Any individual who modifies their personal vehicle for the purpose of actively deceiving the community can face serious consequences up to and including criminal charges.

title: Assault investigation at licensed premise results in charges: C26-191112
content:
Three security personnel are facing charges following an investigation into an assault that left a 28-year-old man with injuries after a disturbance at a licensed premise in downtown Winnipeg.
On August 3, 2026, at approximately 1:00 a.m., the Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) responded to a report of a disturbance in the 400 block of Main Street.
Central District General Patrol officers attended and learned that a 28-year-old patron was involved in a physical altercation with security personnel. He later attended hospital, where he was treated for injuries received during the altercation.
The Major Crimes Unit assumed responsibility for the investigation. As a result, three security personnel, aged 35, 37, and 58, were identified as being involved in the assault.
On August 12, 2026, all three security personnel attended Winnipeg Police Service Headquarters and were arrested. They are facing charges of Assault Causing Bodily Harm and were released on Undertakings.
Anyone with information, or who may have dashcam, security, or cell phone video from around the time of the incident, is asked to contact the Major Crimes Unit at 204-986-6219 or anonymously at Crime Stoppers 204-786-TIPS or
winnipegcrimestoppers.org
